faithful_choreography.observation: B row 1 column 1 is severely corrupted: most of the dancer/body is missing or reduced to fragments, so the opening pose in A is not faithfully reproduced.
B row 5 column 3 is also severely degraded/ghosted, with the head/torso washed out and the body pose only partially readable.

Several poses appear phase-shifted or reordered relative to A. For example, B row 2 columns 1-2 resemble adjacent/source poses but not in the same exact row/column order, and later lunge/lean poses appear in different sampled positions. The overall dance vocabulary is similar, but frame-by-frame timing is not nearly identical.

wardrobe.observation: The main wardrobe is mostly correct: black shiny suit, white shirt, dark tie/suspenders. However, in some B frames the tie/suspenders and shirt details differ or become simplified/washed out.
The two heavily corrupted frames in B lose substantial wardrobe information, especially row 1 column 1 and row 5 column 3.

background.observation: B keeps the same plain studio background, but it is slightly more pale green/gray compared with A's cleaner white/gray backdrop.
The corrupted frames introduce visible artifact blobs/ghosting against the background.

camera_framing.observation: Most frames preserve the full-body, centered, contact-sheet framing, but some figures in B are slightly shifted or scaled differently from the corresponding A frames.
The two corrupted frames break framing continuity because the dancer is not cleanly visible as a full body.

retro_low_budget_dance_video_look.observation: The blank studio, shiny suit, and simple dance-video staging are largely preserved.
AI-like degradation/ghosting in B makes several sampled frames look less like the clean retro source and more artifacted than the original low-budget video aesthetic.

notes: Minor face/identity differences were not materially penalized except where the face/body is visibly missing or corrupted.
No wrong scene or wrong costume was observed; deductions are mainly for corrupted frames and frame-by-frame timing/pose mismatches.

uncertainty_due_to_sampled_frames.reason: The sheets sample every 1/6 second, so exact between-frame motion cannot be judged. Some pose mismatches could be adjacent-frame timing offsets, but the severe corrupted frames and visible ordering differences are directly observable in the sampled frames.
